description: A p5.js reader for a synthetic class mastery heatmap in which learners tell a concept the whole class struggles with (a dark column) from a student who struggles broadly (a dark row), and reweight the at-risk roster's three signals to see how the ranking changes.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Reading a class mastery heatmap and computing an at-risk score
learningObjectives: The learner will distinguish a concept that most of a class struggles with from a student who struggles broadly, by reading the dark columns and dark rows of a heatmap and by computing an at-risk score.
prerequisites: Mastery estimates as model outputs (Chapters 18 and 19)

accessibility.notes: Cell values are printed in the cells as well as shaded; sequential single-hue blue scale; patterns are marked with dashed outlines and text; sliders are native controls with aria labels

controls.label: Weight on low mastery
controls.purpose: Weight of (1 - mean mastery) in the risk score

controls.label: Weight on inactivity
controls.purpose: Weight of days idle / max days idle

controls.label: Weight on prerequisite gaps
controls.purpose: Weight of the prerequisite gap ratio

controls.label: Show the pattern
controls.purpose: Outline the weak column and the weak row

controls.label: Quiz me
controls.purpose: Ask for the concept to re-teach, then the broadly struggling student

controls.label: Heatmap cells and roster rows
controls.purpose: Show estimates; select a student; answer the quiz

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Pattern recognition with a two-question check and a transparent score breakdown
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Scan, quiz, reveal the pattern, inspect one student's signals, reweight
keyQuestions: What does a dark column suggest a teacher change, compared with a dark row?
Which three signals make up the risk score, and how much does each contribute?
Can a single severe signal push a student to the top of the roster?
commonMisconceptions: A dark cell is a measured fact about the student
The top of the roster is always the weakest student academically
The default weights are a validated standard
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz: choose the concept to re-teach and the broadly struggling student
Hand calculation of a risk score checked against the breakdown
Written caution about acting on model estimates

simulation.modelType: Weighted composite score over synthetic data
variables: mastery estimate per student and concept
equations: risk = wM x (1 - mean mastery) + wI x (days idle / 10) + wP x gap ratio
gap ratio = concepts with a prerequisite below 0.6 / 8
assumptions: Synthetic section of 12 students and 8 concepts from a fixed seed
0.6 is the prototype dashboard's pass line
Default weights 0.45/0.30/0.25 are the prototype's choices
limitations: Shades are model estimates, not measured facts
